Roofing in Coppell, Texas

Coppell posts its permits for anyone to read, including the roof jobs. Call one free number any hour and get connected with an independent roofing company that takes Coppell calls.

Coppell's 2018 hail morning

For roofing in Coppell, TX, June 6, 2018 is the date people still mention. CBS News reported that some of the largest hail reports from that early morning storm came from Coppell and Carrollton.

NBC DFW spoke with a Coppell homeowner whose roof, less than three years old, had to be replaced along with siding and gutters. Across the metro, the Insurance Council of Texas expected as many as 20,000 home claims and 25,000 auto claims, with early insured losses around $425 million. A catastrophe modeler later put the total near $1 billion, mostly to roofs, windows, skylights and solar panels.

DFW Expert Roofers is a free phone line, not a roofing company. When you call, an automated assistant takes the details and transfers you to an independent, locally owned roofer that takes Coppell calls.

A suburb built in about twenty years

Coppell was a small farming community until DFW Airport opened next door. According to the Handbook of Texas, the population went from 1,751 in 1981 to 3,826 by 1984, then to roughly 17,000 by 1990 and about 36,000 by 2000. By 2000, nearly all of the land zoned for homes had been built on. The 2020 census counted 42,983 people.

That means much of Coppell was framed within the same two decades, and many of those houses have already had at least one new roof. Coppell sits mainly in Dallas County, with a small area in the far north reaching into Denton County.

1980s homes

Built in the first wave. Find out the number of shingle layers, and whether decking has been replaced before.

1990s homes

Likely on a second roof. If that roof went on after 2018, keep its warranty paperwork where you can find it.

Newer infill

Fewer in number, since the city was nearly built out by 2000. Builder warranty terms may still apply.

Read Coppell's permit reports before you hire

Coppell publishes a monthly list of permits issued by work class. Residential reroofs show up every month, often with a short description of the work. That makes it a useful reference when you compare quotes.

  1. Open a recent month. Find the "Permits Issued by Work Class" report in the city's Document Center.
  2. Look at the reroof lines. Typical scopes read like "tear-off and replacement of existing roofing system, new underlayment, drip edge, flashing and architectural asphalt shingles."
  3. Compare with your quote. If your quote is missing underlayment, drip edge or flashing, ask why.
  4. Check the contractor. Anyone pulling a permit must be registered with the city first. Ask for the registered company name.
  5. Call with questions. Building Inspections: 972-304-3500.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Questions for a Coppell roofer

  • Are you registered with the City of Coppell, and under what name?
  • Will you pull a permit for my reroof, and when will I see it?
  • Does your quote list underlayment, drip edge, flashing and vents by name?
  • How do you price decking you replace, and will you photograph it first?
  • Will your insurance agent send me a current liability certificate?
  • Where is a roof you finished in Coppell that I can drive past?

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

Coppell roofing questions

Must a Coppell roofing company be registered with the city?

Yes, if the job needs a permit. Coppell's construction code says any person or firm doing work that requires a permit must first register with the city as a contractor. A homeowner working on their own homestead can register for their own work. Ask the roofer for the company name it registered under and match it to your contract. Our guide on checking a Texas roofer lists other records to request.

Is a permit required for roofing in Coppell TX?

Roofing is on the list of permits on the city's website, and the city asks you to call Building Inspections at 972-304-3500 for the requirements. The city's monthly permit reports show residential reroof permits issued every month. Before you sign, ask the roofer whether it will pull a permit for your job and when you will see it.

My Coppell roof was replaced after the 2018 hail. Should it be checked?

It is worth asking for a look after any strong storm, and a roof put on in 2018 is now about eight years into its life. Hail bruises are often too small to spot from the driveway. A roofer can document what it finds with photos so you can decide, with your insurer, whether anything needs a claim. For what a thorough check should include, see the roof inspection page.

How does the free roofing line work for Coppell homes?

You call, and an automated assistant answers at any hour. It asks whether the call is about a roof, what is going on and where the house is, then puts you through to an independent, locally owned roofing company that works in Coppell. The line itself never inspects, quotes or repairs, and it costs you nothing. The roofer may pay the line a referral fee.
